description: Canonical interoperability, identity, ownership, persistence, lineage, and semantic contracts for A.R.I.A. This file is the authoritative cross-system contract for Core. Registries own controlled vocabulary, schemas own persisted record validation, reasoning engines own behavior, and explanatory documents describe the architecture without redefining it.

authority.external_corpus_policy: Global and Manufacturers contain technical source and knowledge corpus material. They do not redefine Core contracts.

constitution.responsibility: Defines ARIA's purpose, mission, governing principles, behavioral boundaries, and immutable architectural intent.

core_contract.responsibility: Defines universal identity, interoperability, persistence boundaries, shared semantics, and cross-system invariants.

registries.responsibility: Own controlled semantic vocabularies and stable registry-definition codes.

must_not: invent controlled vocabulary already owned by a Registry

reasoning_engines.responsibility: Define deterministic and probabilistic reasoning behavior, transitions, calculations, routing, validation, orchestration, and learning behavior.
must_not: silently promote model output into authoritative state

explanatory_architecture.responsibility: Explain architecture, reasoning semantics, technical boundaries, and intended behavior in human-readable form.

technical_corpus.responsibility: Provide technical source material, reference knowledge, manufacturer documentation, field knowledge, and domain corpus.
must_not: silently establish canonical truth without provenance and validation

core_principles.technical_mission: ARIA is a technical reasoning resource. Business, customer, person, project, and organizational context may be represented only where it materially supports the technical mission.
core_principles.canonical_identity: Every persisted first-class runtime object has one stable canonical typed identifier.
core_principles.typed_uuid_identity: Runtime canonical identifiers use a defined lowercase prefix followed by an underscore and globally unique UUID. UUIDv7 is preferred.
core_principles.registry_runtime_separation: Registry-definition codes identify vocabulary entries. They are not runtime canonical object identifiers.
core_principles.knowledge_reuse: Reusable technical concepts are created once and referenced. Manufacturer, product, scope, customer, user, project, and case context shall not cause unnecessary duplication.
core_principles.observation_interpretation_separation: Observed information remains distinguishable from interpretation, inference, hypothesis, conclusion, and learned knowledge.
core_principles.source_claim_knowledge_separation: A source, a claim extracted from that source, a normalized semantic relationship, and a persisted Knowledge Graph edge are distinct architectural objects.
core_principles.case_experience_separation: A diagnostic case is an investigation. An Experience Ledger record is validated learning derived from qualifying historical case information. A case is not itself an experience record.
core_principles.probability_confidence_separation: Probability represents estimated likelihood. Confidence represents trust in the quality, support, reliability, or calibration of information or reasoning.
core_principles.lifecycle_reasoning_state_separation: A case's broad lifecycle status and its current reasoning state are separate dimensions.
core_principles.provenance_required: Material technical information must retain sufficient provenance to explain where it came from and how it was transformed.
core_principles.independent_corroboration: Repeated representations of one underlying source do not become independent evidence merely because they appear in multiple artifacts or records.
core_principles.explicit_relationships: Semantic relationships are explicit first-class assertions. Reverse semantics shall not be assumed unless the relationship Registry defines symmetry or an inverse.
core_principles.validated_learning: Historical interaction does not automatically become learned experience. Learning requires appropriate validation and eligibility.
core_principles.model_non_authority: A language model may interpret, propose, classify, summarize, and reason. It does not independently own authoritative state, canonical truth, probabilities, validated outcomes, or permanent knowledge.
core_principles.append_only_history: Material case events, probability changes, route history, evidence history, validation outcomes, and learning lineage shall remain auditable rather than being silently overwritten.
core_principles.unknown_is_valid: Unknown, missing, unresolved, unavailable, and not-applicable states shall remain representable. ARIA shall not manufacture certainty to fill information gaps.

identifier_contract.specialized_entity_rule: Use the most specific established runtime identity prefix when one exists. Use ent_<UUID> only for reusable canonical technical entities without a dedicated prefix.

non_runtime_registry_codes.description: Registry-definition codes are stable vocabulary keys. They are not runtime canonical identities.

identifier_contract.legacy_policy: Legacy identifiers may be preserved for migration and auditability but shall not remain authoritative runtime identity.

registry_contract.purpose: Registries own controlled vocabulary and semantic catalog definitions.
rules: A Registry may define type names, canonical labels, categories, inverses, defaults, semantic rules, or static technical catalog definitions.
A Registry code shall not be used as the identifier of a runtime case object.
A runtime action instance uses act_<UUID> even when its action_type references ACT-RF-003.
A canonical failure-mode entity uses fm_<UUID> even when its classification originates from FM-RF-001.
A canonical symptom entity uses sym_<UUID> even when its catalog definition originates from SYM-RF-003.
Schemas and engines shall reference Registry vocabulary rather than reproducing independent lists.
Registry vocabulary changes must be deliberate and auditable.

fields.created_at: When the ARIA record was created.
fields.updated_at: When the persisted record was most recently materially updated.
fields.observed_at: When the underlying technical condition was actually observed.
fields.recorded_at: When an observation or statement was recorded.
fields.valid_from: Beginning of known applicability or validity.
fields.valid_to: End of known applicability or validity.
fields.superseded_at: When the object or assertion was superseded.

rules: Observed time and recorded time are not interchangeable.
Record creation time does not imply technical occurrence time.
Current knowledge shall not automatically be applied retroactively when historical applicability differs.
Superseded information may remain historically valid.

confidence_contract.description: Confidence expresses trust in quality, support, reliability, calibration, or applicability. Confidence is not probability.
rules: Confidence values shall not imply precision unsupported by the evidence.
Different confidence dimensions shall not be collapsed into one generic number when that would hide material uncertainty.
Confidence may be high while hypothesis probability remains low.
Probability may be high while confidence in that probability remains low.

probability_contract.description: Probability expresses current estimated likelihood within a defined reasoning model.
rules: Probability and confidence are separately persisted.
Mutually exclusive hypotheses may be normalized within a defined probability group.
Coexisting hypotheses are not required to sum to one.
Unknown probability mass may be preserved.
Historical frequency primarily informs priors.
Current validated evidence primarily informs posterior updates.
Probability changes must remain explainable and auditable.

provenance_contract.description: Canonical lineage contract for technical information.
rules: Derived information retains lineage to its parent information.
Summaries and transformations do not become independent sources merely because their text differs.
Model inference must be marked as inferred lineage.
Provenance describes lineage; source authority is evaluated separately.

authority_contract.description: Authority evaluates how strongly a source should govern a particular technical question within applicable context.
rules: Authority is contextual, not universal.
Manufacturer documentation may be authoritative for design intent but does not establish what physically occurred in a specific field case.
Direct measurement may establish observed behavior without rewriting design requirements.
Historical frequency may inform probability without overriding deterministic technical requirements.
Newer documentation shall not automatically supersede older documentation when the older material remains applicable to the relevant revision.
Authority, confidence, probability, and applicability are separate concepts.

artifact_contract.description: A concrete digital or physical source-bearing artifact such as a PDF, screenshot, configuration export, photograph, log file, video, manual, drawing, or other retrievable technical object.
rules: An artifact is not automatically a logical technical source.
Multiple artifacts may represent the same source.
The same artifact may support multiple claims.
Artifact storage location is not canonical technical identity.

source_contract.description: A logical technical source from which claims, observations, requirements, or other technical information originate.
rules: A source identifies origin, not automatically truth.
A source may contain multiple independent claims.
Source authority depends on technical question and applicability.
Source identity shall not be replaced by a filesystem path.

claim_contract.description: A proposition asserted, extracted, reported, derived, or inferred from one or more sources or observations.
rules: Claims preserve what was asserted before canonical normalization.
A claim is not automatically canonical technical truth.
Multiple claims may normalize to one semantic relationship.
Conflicting claims may coexist until reconciled.
A claim extracted by a language model remains candidate information until accepted by applicable validation logic.

canonical_entity_contract.description: Reusable technical concept represented independently from case-specific observations.
rules: Names are not identity.
Aliases are not automatically separate canonical entities.
A canonical entity shall not embed case-specific observation history.
Relationships shall not be hidden inside arbitrary metadata when graph semantics materially matter.
Canonical entities may be reused across manufacturers, products, cases, customers, teams, and users where technically appropriate.

relationship_contract.description: First-class semantic assertion connecting eligible canonical ARIA objects. Relationships may be reusable, case-specific, evidentiary, experiential, procedural, or contextual.
rules: Relationship vocabulary is owned exclusively by the relationship Registry.
A reverse relationship is not assumed unless the Registry defines symmetry or an inverse.
Relationship confidence is not hypothesis probability.
Case-specific relationships do not automatically become reusable Knowledge Graph edges.
A reusable Knowledge Graph edge may correspond to a semantic relationship without sharing its identifier.

knowledge_graph_contract.description: Reusable canonical technical graph built from validated technical concepts and relationships.

rules: A Knowledge Graph node projects a canonical technical entity into reusable graph structure.
Knowledge nodes do not replace canonical entity identity.
Knowledge Graph edges represent reusable validated graph structure.
Knowledge edges shall not store transient case reasoning as permanent technical truth.
Knowledge edges use Registry relationship semantics.
A Knowledge Graph edge and a general semantic relationship are distinct records.

promotion_gate.rule: No case-specific observation, model inference, or Experience Ledger pattern silently becomes canonical Knowledge Graph truth.

case_contract.description: A diagnostic or technical investigation with preserved evolving state.

lifecycle_status_semantics.description: Broad case lifecycle. Detailed diagnostic phase belongs in reasoning_state.
lifecycle_status_semantics.registry_rule: Final controlled values shall be owned by the applicable case lifecycle Registry or schema, not duplicated by reasoning engines.

rules: Case lifecycle status and reasoning state are separate.
A case is not itself an Experience Ledger record.
Case history shall not be erased when reasoning reroutes.
New evidence updates the current case state rather than restarting the investigation.
A case may contain multiple simultaneous failure modes.
Case closure does not automatically establish learning eligibility.

context_contract.description: Resolved multidimensional technical context applicable to a case, claim, relationship, source, experience, or reasoning operation.
rules: Context dimensions and contextual values are different concepts.
Context may reference canonical entities instead of duplicating them.
Unknown context remains explicitly unknown.
Missing context shall only be requested when expected to materially improve reasoning.
Context similarity is not binary and may be dimension-specific.

event_contract.description: Immutable record of a material occurrence affecting case state, reasoning, external input, execution, or system behavior.
rules: Events are append-only.
Events shall identify their originating case when case-specific.
Events may trigger reasoning but do not themselves replace authoritative case state.
Repeated ingestion of the same stable external event should be idempotent.

evidence_contract.description: Case-specific observed, measured, reported, recorded, or derived information used during reasoning.
rules: Evidence and interpretation remain distinguishable.
Evidence may reference canonical entities without becoming those entities.
Derived evidence retains parent lineage.
Duplicate representations of the same underlying observation shall not count as independent corroboration.
Evidence reliability is not hypothesis probability.
Evidence status vocabulary shall be owned in one Registry or schema rather than independently by engines.

hypothesis_contract.description: Case-specific candidate explanation evaluating a canonical failure mode, cause, condition, or other technically meaningful explanation.
rules: A hypothesis instance is distinct from the canonical entity being evaluated.
Historical priors are not current case evidence.
Probability history shall remain auditable.
Hypothesis status vocabulary shall have one canonical owner.
A hypothesis is not promoted directly into Knowledge Graph truth.

action_contract.description: A runtime diagnostic, inspection, verification, measurement, corrective, informational, validation, or operational action.
rules: Registry action code identifies action definition; act_<UUID> identifies runtime action instance.
Action completion and action effectiveness are separate.
An action may produce evidence and outcomes.
Repeated actions require a technical justification when an equivalent valid result already exists.
Safety, authorization, access, and service-impact gates may prohibit execution.

route_step_contract.description: Persisted diagnostic routing decision or route-history step.
rules: Route history is append-only.
A route step records why a diagnostic next hop was chosen.
Route selection is not equivalent to hypothesis probability.
Failed or low-yield routes remain useful historical information.

outcome_contract.description: Recorded result of an action, test, observation interval, validation step, learning decision, or case disposition.
rules: Action completion and technical success are separate outcomes.
Condition improvement is not equivalent to validated resolution.
A validation outcome is not automatically proof of exact causal mechanism.
Outcome records preserve what actually occurred rather than what was predicted.

experience_contract.description: Validated historical learning derived from qualifying case history or other explicitly eligible validated observations.
rules: A case is not an Experience Ledger record.
Experience must retain source case lineage.
Experience shall preserve relevant technical context.
Learning weight depends on evidence quality, attribution quality, validation, context completeness, and applicable learning policy.
Experience may influence priors, route performance, contextual similarity, and candidate knowledge.
Experience shall not silently rewrite canonical technical truth.
User-specific learning remains scoped to the relevant user and context.
One case does not establish a universal causal rule.

user_contract.description: Technical participant identity used when user-specific experience, capability, provenance, responsibility, or reasoning context is materially relevant.
rules: User identity exists only where technically useful.
Reporter identity does not establish fault attribution.
User-specific history may influence priors or routing only when validated and contextually relevant.
ARIA shall not become an HR performance system.

stages.meaning: What a source or observation asserts.
Normalized semantic assertion using canonical entities and Registry relationship vocabulary.

rules: Not every artifact requires a distinct logical source.
Not every claim becomes a semantic relationship.
Not every semantic relationship becomes reusable Knowledge Graph knowledge.
Every transformation retains lineage.
Contradictory claims may coexist until appropriately resolved.
The sequence is conceptual rather than a mandatory fixed workflow.
ARIA is event-driven and may revisit reasoning functions as state changes.
Not every case requires every object type.
Reasoning resumes from current authoritative state.
Validated completed experience may later influence future cases.

decision_routing_boundary.principle: Decision determines comparative diagnostic utility. Routing determines path progression and operational next-hop history.
decision_engine: evaluates cost, risk, discrimination, and expected utility
routing_engine: selects and records next hop from eligible scored actions
decision_routing_boundary.rule: Decision and Routing may exchange scores and candidates but shall not independently implement two competing utility models.

validation_learning_boundary.principle: Validation establishes what the evidence supports. Learning determines what validated history is allowed to teach.
rules: Symptom resolution does not automatically prove root cause.
Operational recovery may be validated while causal confidence remains limited.
Validation determines learning restrictions.
Learning Engine applies those restrictions when creating Experience Ledger records.
Knowledge promotion remains a separate governance action.
HYPOTHESIS_PROBABILITY is a probability dimension, not a confidence dimension.
Evidence quality is confidence-related metadata.
Diagnostic confidence evaluates sufficiency of evidence for a diagnosis.
Causal confidence evaluates support for causal attribution.
Resolution confidence evaluates support for successful resolution.
Learning confidence evaluates whether historical information is safe to influence future reasoning.
Context-match confidence evaluates technical applicability of retrieved information.

persistent_state_policy.authoritative_state: Structured persisted services, not conversational model output.
rules: Partial multi-object reasoning updates should be transactionally consistent.
Concurrent state writes must not silently overwrite newer state.
External event ingestion should support idempotency.
Model-generated proposals require structured-service acceptance before becoming authoritative state.

promotion_rules: Contradictions shall be preserved or resolved.
Causal claims require stronger validation than simple association.
Repeated experience may propose canonical knowledge but does not independently authorize it.

technical_scope_boundary.rule: These contextual concepts may exist only to support technical reasoning, provenance, applicability, experience, or execution. Core shall not evolve into CRM, HR, accounting, sales, or general business-management architecture.

rules: entity_contracts.json remains temporarily until all dependent Core files reference core_contracts.json.
No existing schema shall be considered final until reconciled against this contract.
No existing reasoning engine shall be considered final until its vocabulary ownership and persistence boundaries are reconciled.
No explanatory Markdown file shall be considered final until its authority references and semantics align with this contract.
The final migration step shall remove superseded contracts only after repository-wide validation.

global_invariants: One controlled vocabulary owner per semantic domain.
One canonical identity system.
Registry codes are not runtime IDs.
Runtime IDs use typed UUID identity.
Case status and reasoning state are separate.
Case and Experience Ledger records are separate.
Source and artifact are separate.
Source and claim are separate.
Claim and canonical relationship are separate.
Semantic relationship and Knowledge Graph edge are separate.
Observation and interpretation are separate.
Probability and confidence are separate.
Authority and confidence are separate.
Applicability and authority are separate.
Action completion and action success are separate.
Symptom resolution and causal proof are separate.
Historical frequency and technical causality are separate.
Repeated representations of one source are not independent corroboration.
Unknown information remains representable.
Context shall not create unnecessary canonical duplication.
Model output is proposal until accepted by structured services.
Case evidence does not silently rewrite canonical knowledge.
Experience does not silently rewrite canonical knowledge.
Deprecated and superseded knowledge remains historically traceable.
Global and Manufacturers are technical corpus, not architectural authority.
ARIA remains a technical reasoning resource.
